cells.tense: Your hands are open right now, and what you have moves toward where it runs short.
cells.act: choose which star to steer by and steer
cells.ask: Pick one person you already help, and name to yourself what you want their year to move toward. Then let this week's help follow that.
cells.core:
Someone near you is short of what you have, and you take in the whole shape of it — the gap, the handoff, what closes it. You do that without a speech, and they come out steadier for it. That is strength on its way out of you, by measure, not spilling. It goes well where you can be generous without keeping a tally, where it doesn't dim you, and where the one receiving it ends up more able rather than smaller.

Pick one person you already help and say to yourself what you want their life to point toward — not just this week's repair. Then let what you hand over follow that. Help gets lighter when it has a direction to travel in, and you'll spot sooner the point where it stopped being a gift and became a job.
cells.sheetLine: Your strength goes where it's short, and no one has to ask twice.
cells.place: where the pattern shows, apart from any one case

cells.tense: The whole map of who will run short is running ahead of you, and you will have supplies matched before anyone speaks.
cells.act: act on the private sense of what is right
cells.ask: When you notice yourself totting up what someone is owed, make the small fair call and keep it to yourself. No explanation after.
cells.core:
You can see a need coming before it lands — who will run short, what it costs, where the hole opens. That sight is real. It has also started deciding for you, so you show up with the answer built and no room left for whoever is actually there. The generosity is intact; it just moves faster than the situation does, and now and then it spends something you needed on a case you forecast.

When the totting-up starts, make the small fair call you already feel and say nothing about it. That private compass doesn't need a case argued. Holding the strength back instead of pressing it out is the practice here — one quiet fair call, kept quiet, no follow-up speech.
cells.sheetLine: You see who'll come up short and you've started deciding for them.

cells.tense: You gave what you had where it was needed, and the handing over ran on past the point where you were met.
cells.act: engage the hard part on purpose and see what holds
cells.ask: Take the piece of this you've been going around, and stay with it once, on purpose. Keep what you're committed to; the way you've been doing it can go.
cells.core:
The pattern still reads clear to you — you see what's needed about as well as you ever did — but nothing underneath it is pushing the strength out anymore. The help leaves you flatter now, in a way you don't bring up, and toward some people you give to, you've quit expecting much back. What used to feed all this was finishing something, and lately a lot has been started toward others with nothing closed.

Go at the hard piece you've been routing around, once, deliberately. Not more effort and not more feeling — commitment tested against friction is what puts strength back in your hands. Keep the commitment; let go of the approach, of the method you reached for. Those may be two different things.

cells.tense: You are holding the whole pattern level, and you would tell anyone it simply holds that way.
cells.act: turn toward the one direction and stop surveying
cells.ask: Take the thing you want, not what the situation wants, and keep that heading for three days. Don't take its measure in between.
cells.core:
You keep people supplied, and you read the board well enough that it looks like nothing. Habit, you'd say, if asked. The level floor in your circle has your hands in it, and reading the situation well is part of how you place what you have. That is strength leaving you, outward. It only goes unseen by you; the ones who take it up have noticed right along.

Take the thing you want, rather than what the moment seems to need, and hold that heading for three days. Don't check how it's measuring up along the way. Having something of your own to move toward is what keeps the offering steady — and if you keep it in view, the ones around you tend to steady up too.
cells.sheetLine: You say it just holds. The ones taking it up know better.
cells.place: where the pattern shows, apart from any one case

attempts.check: The undrawn claim: I read the Too Much cell as a person carrying the whole pattern in their head, matching supply against demand before either moves. The record does not support that as history — only as a bend that capacity can take now — so I describe the mechanism, not its origin. A reader could object that they are not surveying anyone's need but hiding from their own; the ask still works either way, because a private count does not need the other person's agreement to be done. The sentence that serves me more than them: 'You are the one keeping it all level.' I have cut it.
